newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee shipments said hurt by strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee shipments said hurt by strike.

text.p: Shipments of coffee to Colombia's ports have been adversely affected by the nationwide public workers' strike that began early Tuesday, a senior coffee official said.

John Naranjo, commercial manager of the National Coffee Growers' Federation, said he was unable to give an exact estimate of the extent to which the strike would delay exports. But he stressed that "the handling of coffee in ports has diminished."

"It hasn't been possible to transport coffee the way we would have liked," Naranjo said, adding that an average of just 10 truckloads of coffee had reached Colombia's main ports as of 1100 local time on Tuesday, well below the average daily flow.

Neither port workers nor cargo haulers have joined in the strike by government workers. But the threat of roadblocks and vandalism by leftist guerrillas supporting the strike was apparently keeping many truckers off the nation's highways.
Naranjo said coffee shipments would be hurt furhter as long as the strike holds but he declined further comment.
